issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The feature filter ranks columns by |Spearman| against y using only the training fold's Xtr. The test features (Xte) are only column-sliced with the same indices, and no test labels or files are used.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. Columns with zero variance get a score of 0 through the den guard. rankdata(axis=0) gives per-column ranks. The same column indices are applied to train and test. The diff refers to y but does not define it; y must already be defined earlier in fit_predict, because the unchanged m.fit(..., y) uses it.

The numbers support rejecting. The candidate's loss of 0.4787 is 0.0042 worse than the incumbent's 0.4745 (lower is better). That difference is well within noise, and there is only one run on each side.

Recomputed z = (0.4745 - 0.4787) / (0.0070 * sqrt(2)) = -0.424, close to the harness's -0.419. The small gap is probably from rounding or a slightly different sd estimate. The decision is the same either way.
Minor: hard-coding 400 kept columns is a new hyperparameter, and it gave no measurable gain, so dropping it also keeps the code simpler.
